messages:
jamie_prod: Heads up — several EU customers report embeddings calls routed to us-east, huge latency spikes (600ms -> 2s) and some downstream failures. Not sure why routing drifted.

mike_support: Can you share an example request/response + request_id? Which endpoint/model and region were you targeting?

jamie_prod: Example below (redacted). Request includes region=eu-west-1 but response contains routed_region: us-east-1 and longer tail.
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  \"model\": \"embed-analog-1\",
  \"region\": \"eu-west-1\",
  \"input\": [\"check routing\"]
}
```
Response snippet:
```json
{\"request_id\": \"cid_0a1b2c3d\", \"routed_region\": \"us-east-1\", \"latency_ms\": 1789}
```
deploy-bot: Routing policy escalation: fallback routing triggered (eu-west-1 -> us-east-1) due to capacity threshold breach at 2026-03-17T09:12:43Z.

beth_sre: Looking at infra metrics — eu-west GPU pool hit 87% alloc and coldstart queue spiked. The spill/fallback threshold (0.8) was exceeded so policy routed to other region. Also saw autoscaler lag on warmup. Two notes: 1) immediate mitigation is to pin the endpoint to eu-west or disable cross-region fallback, 2) batching config in eu-west is smaller which increased per-request coldstart pressure.

elaine_eng: Workaround to pin endpoint (temporary):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/endpoints/ENDPOINT_ID/config \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{"routing": {"force_region": "eu-west-1", "fallback": false}}'
```
This forces local routing (customers will see queuing if local capacity saturates).

mike_support: Please run this repro curl and paste the full response with request_id so we can correlate logs:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{"model":"embed-analog-1","input":["routing test"],"region":"eu-west-1"}'
```

jamie_prod: Pasted the full response for cid_0a1b2c3d. Also noticed some responses returned embedding vectors with dim 1536 while our indexer expects 768 — seems the fallback routed to a different model variant in us-east. That caused downstream errors.

beth_sre: Confirmed: fallback mapping used a higher-capacity variant in us-east (embed-analog-1-xl) resulting in 1536 dims. That's a compatibility issue. Immediate fixes: 1) update fallback map to only allow compatible variants; 2) set endpoint routing.fallback=false to prevent cross-region replacement; 3) align max_batch_size across clusters (set max_batch_size=32) to reduce coldstart churn. We'll apply the routing policy change in ~15 minutes.

mike_support: Opening internal escalation ticket INFRA-2982 and cc'ing SRE+Infra. I'll notify affected customers with suggested mitigation (pin region or expect transient queuing).

jamie_prod: Applying the pin now and monitoring. Will post updated metrics in 10m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

beth_sre: Follow-up: we'll provision additional reserved capacity for eu-west and add a guardrail to prevent incompatible variant fallback. Long-term: improve per-model compatibility matrix for cross-region fallbacks.

mike_support: Thanks — collecting final logs from you @jamie_prod and will close once SRE confirms policy change and customer acknowledgement.
